Independent Villain.name: Independent Villain
Independent Villain.description:
🕶️ You are a criminal who answers to no group: jobs through brokers, gear from the black market, and the law one mistake behind you.

⚖️ A criminal. If caught, you face custody, trial and, for serious villains, Tartarus. The story start sets whether police know your face.
🏫 A cover life with a job, a room and a name; jobs through brokers such as Giran; then lying low and watching the news for your description.
⚠️ No orders, only debts: broker fees, favors owed, rent on safe rooms, and everyone you have crossed.
🔓 Learnable later: Fallback Hideout, Untraceable Job.

📈 Grants: Speed +1, Streetwise +10, Stealth +10, Negotiation +5
⚡ Starting technique: Broker's Number
🎒 Starts with: Villain coat and gear, Burner phone, Forged ID, ¥20,000, Go-bag, Casual clothes
Independent Villain.traitNarrativeEffects:
Legal status: criminal, solo or in short-lived crews. Quirk use on people, theft, smuggling, carrying weapons are crimes; capture: custody, trial, Tartarus for serious villains. Story start sets whether police know their face.
Access: brokers (e.g. Giran) selling jobs, gear, introductions; black markets (weapons, forged papers, Trigger); cheap rooms, lockers in Hosu and elsewhere under the forged ID; gang and yakuza turf, if they pay respect.
Obligations: no orders, only debts: broker fees, favors, rent, everyone they crossed.
Who notices: brokers, rivals, gangs; Quirk-crime detectives; patrolling heroes; bigger groups' recruiters.
Standing pressures: Hero Killer Stain (killed or crippled dozens of 'fake' pro heroes) is at large as the year opens; police jumpy at hero sightings near crimes; new groups pay well for muscle; yakuza remnants push Quirk-boosting Trigger; heroes and police short-staffed; more jobs than takers.
Typical week: cover life, jobs, lying low.
